episodes.202069: Heavy rainfall over a 3-4 hour period led to widespread flash and nuisance flooding across portions of Limestone and Madison Counties during the afternoon and early evening hours of the 22nd. Several roads were closed and numerous families had to be evacuated from their homes and apartments during the flooding in Harvest in Madison County, AL. 6-12 of water affected the apartments in Harvest, forcing residents to require assistance in leaving their homes during the event. No injuries or fatalities were reported.
episodes.202119: An approaching cold front caused two rounds of thunderstorms to track through central and east-central Wisconsin during the early afternoon and again late in the afternoon into the early evening on Monday (6/23).  The storms produced damaging winds and a death in Green Bay when a tree fell on a 9-year-old child.
episodes.202227: A line of thunderstorms produced strong winds over the southern bay of Green Bay during the afternoon hours on Monday (6/23).
episodes.202410: An early season plume of monsoon moisture advected northward into New Mexico from June 22nd through the 24th bringing several days of flash flooding and severe weather across portions of northern and central NM. June 22nd in particular saw severe thunderstorms produce numerous severe wind gusts of 60 mph or stronger across eastern NM from Roswell to Nara Visa with reports of downed utility poles and arcing powerlines near Roswell and dust being kicked up in Quay County. Heavy rains also produced flash flooding reports in Roswell where multiple cars and a fire truck were stuck in deep water. June 23rd saw thunderstorms bring burn scar flash flooding to the Ruidoso area burn scars where swift water rescues were performed at a mobile home park and a hotel. Flash flooding was also reported along an area where two to three inches or more of rain fell just south of I-40 in eastern NM near Santa Rosa and Newkirk. The Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar saw flash flooding on June 24th from burn scar flash flooding when NM 518 was closed due to flood waters. Heavy rains also produced flash flooding in Belen, NM where debris and high waters washed out a portion of I-25 at mile marker 190 which required cleanup crews to reopen the next day. Monsoon moisture began to lower after the 24th as did the thunderstorm activity by June 25th. ||Key Impacts: Flash flooding, burn scar flash flooding, debris flow, thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.202451: A couple strong to severe lines of thunderstorms moved across southern WI along a stationary front. Damaging winds and flooding occurred.
episodes.202656: During the evening of June 22nd, thunderstorms in New Mexico grew into a line of storms and moved into the western combined Panhandles. These storms formed in a fairly unstable environment and posed a severe threat in to the central to western combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. These storms produced severe wind gusts as several mesonet ground stations recorded severe wind gusts and even up to 65mph.
episodes.202657: During the evening of June 22nd, thunderstorms in New Mexico grew into a line of storms and moved into the western combined Panhandles. These storms formed in a fairly unstable environment and posed a severe threat in to the central to western combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles. These storms produced severe wind gusts as several mesonet ground stations recorded severe wind gusts and even up to 65mph.
episodes.203491: Thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours of June 22nd over Logan, northwestern Custer and Blaine Counties. This activity quickly intensified, becoming severe around 5 PM CDT over Blaine County. Activity persisted over the eastern Sandhills and portions of north central Nebraska into the mid evening hours. This activity produced hail up to 2 inches in diameter. Thunderstorm wind gusts, estimated at 80 MPH, broke a power pole and led to severe tree damage in southwestern Holt County. A second area of severe thunderstorms tracked into the northeastern Panhandle. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 65 MPH were reported in Garden County.
episodes.203544: An area of severe storms pushed into the Brainerd Lakes region just after midnight on the 23rd and pushed to the northeast across the Minnesota Arrowhead while turning into a bow echo. While there were a few hail reports, this system was predominately a wind producer with numerous reports of trees down along the path of the storm. A measured wind gust of 59 mph was recorded near Tamarack.
episodes.203616: A supercell produced damaging winds in eastern Marshall County and two EF-1 tornadoes across northern Beltrami county during the evening hours.
episodes.203631: Afternoon easterly flow sea breeze convection produces gusty marine winds over Tampa Bay and San Carlos Bay area waters.
episodes.203633: Afternoon easterly flow sea breeze thunderstorms produce lightning strike that injures a person at Holmes Beach in Pinellas County.
episodes.203796: A monsoonal weather pattern resulted in scattered thunderstorms across the region. Slow-moving thunderstorms resulted in localized flash flooding in some locations.
episodes.204194: A typical summer pattern allowed for scattered afternoon storms. A few instances of damaging winds and localized flash flooding occurred.
episodes.204305: A surface boundary across northwest Iowa in the morning slowly sunk into central Iowa later in the day. By then, daytime heating resulted in sufficient destabilization for for convective development along the boundary. Surface based CAPE of 2000 J/kg was present across central to southern Iowa, though weaker deep layer shear of 25 kts or less prevent better organization of storms.  Gusty winds of 60 to 65 mph were observed with storms, especially early on in storm development with dry air in the lowest levels. As deep saturation occurred through the late evening and overnight, the primary hazard of concern transitioned from damaging winds to heavy rain. Repeated heavy rain fell across southern portions of Iowa and deep warm cloud layers allowed for efficient rain production. PWAT values were generally in the 2 to 2.3 range and rain totals through late morning on June 24 were from 4 to 6 inches in a band across southern Iowa with isolated totals of 7 to 8 inches or more. Despite these very high rainfall amounts, very little hydrologic issues were reported. This was likely avoided thanks to rain falling across rural areas  with quickly maturing crops able to absorb the heavy rain.
episodes.204386: A summertime pattern continued over the area with scattered thunderstorms. A few storms were strong with wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.204768: During the afternoon and evening on June 23rd, a complex of thunderstorms moved through southeast Minnesota bringing isolated instances of wind damage. Additionally, a 69 mph wind gust was measured in Dexter, Minnesota.
episodes.204769: During the afternoon and evening hours on June 23rd, a complex of storms produced strong winds across west-central Wisconsin that resulted in isolated tree damage in southwest Wisconsin and some overturned boats in Adams County.
episodes.204909: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours of June 23rd across portions of central and south central Kansas. These storms moved north and northeast through the evening hours with additional development through the overnight hours. These storms resulted in hail, wind and flooding reports.
episodes.205140: Thunderstorms produced large hail in southwest Alabama.
episodes.205141: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.205142: Thunderstorms produced high winds as they moved across the Florida panhandle.
